name: Lamar Wise

bio.statement: A Multnomah County release says Wise was appointed to House District 48 on November 5, 2025, and is political director for AFSCME Council 75.
bio.excerpt: political director for Oregon Council 75 of the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees

source.publisher: Multnomah County news release

bio.statement: The Oregon Capital Chronicle described Wise at his appointment as former political director of the state AFSCME union and former executive director of the Oregon Student Association.
bio.excerpt: former executive director of the Oregon Student Association

source.publisher: Oregon Capital Chronicle

bio.statement: OPB, republishing the Capital Chronicle, reports the state ethics commission voted 8-0 to open a full investigation of Wise over an alleged unreported $25,000 stipend.
bio.excerpt: voted 8-0 to open a full investigation into Rep. Lamar Wise, D-Portland

source.publisher: OPB (Oregon Capital Chronicle)

bio.statement: In the same report, Wise says he amended his financial form, called the omission an honest mistake, and expects it to be resolved soon.
bio.excerpt: this honest mistake, and expect it to be resolved soon.

source.publisher: OPB (Oregon Capital Chronicle)

bio.statement: His pamphlet statement lists Wise's occupation as State Representative and Oregon AFSCME project director, a past role as Oregon Student Association executive director, University of Oregon, and the Higher Education Coordinating Commission.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: State Representative; Project Director, Oregon AFSCME Occupational Background: Executive Director, Oregon Student Association Educational Background: University of Oregon Prior Governmental Experience: Higher Education Coordinating Commission

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 55

positions.statement: At his appointment, Wise said he would focus on improving housing and uplifting Oregon's economy, per the Capital Chronicle.
positions.excerpt: improving housing and uplifting Oregon’s economy.

source.publisher: Oregon Capital Chronicle

positions.statement: The Capital Chronicle also reported Wise intends to carry on advocacy for education and reducing chronic absenteeism.
positions.excerpt: advocating for education and reducing Oregon’s chronic absenteeism.

source.publisher: Oregon Capital Chronicle

positions.statement: Wise says in his pamphlet statement that he closed corporate tax loopholes and expanded a tax cut for more than 200,000 families, and wants big corporations to pay their fair share.
positions.excerpt: That’s why I closed corporate tax loopholes and expanded a tax cut for more than 200,000 hard-working families.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 55

positions.statement: Wise's pamphlet statement lists improving education by reducing class sizes, addressing chronic absenteeism and growing affordable childcare programs.
positions.excerpt: IMPROVING EDUCATION by reducing class sizes, addressing chronic absenteeism, and growing affordable childcare programs.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 55

positions.statement: Wise's pamphlet statement lists lowering housing costs by cutting red tape and costs and speeding up housing production.
positions.excerpt: LOWERING HOUSING COSTS by cutting the red tape and costs and speeding up housing production.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 55

positions.statement: Wise's pamphlet statement lists expanding access to mental health care so people can get help instead of ending up on the streets.
positions.excerpt: EXPANDING ACCESS to mental health care so people can get the help they need instead of ending up on the streets.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 55

voting_record.statement: The Portland Tribune reports Wise proposed legislation on chronic absenteeism data; he said the Department of Education should use data it already has.
voting_record.excerpt: We're really asking for the Department of Education to use the data that they already have,

source.publisher: Portland Tribune

collection_notes: Incumbent (appointed 2025) per Multnomah County T1 release; inventory says true, matches. Ethics-investigation items (b3, b4) are included as neutral, balanced by Wise's response; reviewer should decide whether to keep. The OPB URL date is Oct 12; fetch said published Oct 13, so published_at left null. Positions b-quotes 'advocating' / 'improving housing' are partial quotes from the CapChron article. Ballotpedia profile page inconsistently lists predecessor's party; not used. Bio cap (5): pamphlet occupation, background, education and prior experience were combined into one item. No campaign website printed. Pamphlet says Wise would bring down prices and have big corporations pay their fair share (covered in taxes item).
